# MightyStar Facial Reference — Complete AI Handoff

**Prepared: 19 October 2026. Scope: the actual captured reference library, not a newly implemented facial engine.**

## 1. What this handoff contains

This document is the complete text index and technical explanation of the visual library shown in the browser. It covers **50 cached PMX/BPMX model variants, 4,789 morph controls, 19,206 captured images and 422 labeled before/after sheets**. The original Jean study is included. Different outfits are separate model variants and may have different morphs.

**For transfer to another AI, use the companion ZIP package.** The Markdown supplies the full explanations and per-key index; its relative image links require the accompanying `collection/` folder. A text-only AI cannot visually inspect an image merely because its path appears in Markdown. A multimodal AI or an AI with filesystem/image tools should open the linked files. The package is self-contained for reviewing captures; it does not include the original model/texture binaries or an executable app.

- Open `START-HERE.html` in the extracted ZIP to browse the same searchable visual library offline. It redirects to `collection/index.html`.
- Read this handbook for definitions, capture method, per-model caveats and the complete per-key inventory.
- Use `AI-FACIAL-REFERENCE-CATALOG.json` for precise programmatic access to every key, image path, measurement, and adapter mapping.
- Use `implementation-snapshot/` to inspect the current small facial system. These copies are documentation snapshots, not the live source files to edit.
- Use the package manifest to verify the included evidence files.

## 2. Project status and the user’s intended sequence

The user wants a much more expressive AI companion. The agreed first step was to create and review visual references before building a new facial engine. That reference step is complete. **No new expression engine, conversational performance system or production model deformation was implemented in this capture work.** The running app, saved characters, chats and provider credentials were not changed by this reference workflow.

The next engineering work should build on observed controls and calibrated combinations, rather than assuming that ARKit naming or a Japanese/English label guarantees a visual result.

## 3. How another AI should inspect the evidence

1. Choose one exact model variant from the index. Use its cache ID/asset path, not the display name alone.
2. Read that model’s warnings and capture settings. Open its neutral image.
3. Browse its before/after sheets to find candidate controls.
4. Open the individual 480 × 480 images for neutral, 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0. Compare the same region with the same camera.
5. Inspect the oblique image at 1.0 for depth, intersections and hidden geometry. Its camera angle differs, so do not treat it as a pixel-aligned comparison to frontal neutral.
6. Record observed effects separately from interpretations suggested by the key name. Do not invent English translations or assume an author English label is accurate.
7. Treat a key with little visible change as unverified. It may affect hidden geometry, a material, an accessory, or require another control; it is not automatically broken.
8. Inspect and test combinations before proposing expression recipes. These captures activate one control at a time; they do not prove combinations are safe.
9. Inspect animation clips later to evaluate timing and lifelike movement. Still images do not validate transition quality, blinking rhythm, lip sync or conversation-level expression choices.

### Efficient reading

This handbook is intentionally extensive. Search for a model’s ID or exact key name and read one section at a time. Do not attempt to place all images or the entire catalog into one model context. Start with contact sheets, then request individual images.

## 4. Terminology and exact data conventions

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Model variant | One specific PMX/BPMX binary, including its outfit/skin; display names can repeat. |
| Cache ID | The `.asset` filename used by the local cache. Its hexadecimal stem normally hashes the asset identifier/path; it is **not** a checksum of the model bytes. The JSON catalog also records a separately computed binary SHA-256. |
| Morph index | Zero-based position in this exact model’s morph list. Never copy an index from one model to another. |
| Original key | Exact original morph `name`, preserving script, spacing, suffixes and full-width characters. |
| Author English label | The file’s `englishName`; it may be empty, cryptic, duplicated or misleading. |
| Category | Author-provided UI metadata: System=0, Eyebrow=1, Eye=2, Lip=3, Other=4. |
| Morph type | How deformation is applied: group, vertex, bone, UV, material, etc.; it does not identify the facial region. |
| Weight | Requested single-control influence: 0.25, 0.5 or 1.0. These are test samples, not certified safe limits. |
| Neutral | All morph weights set to zero with the sampled skeletal base pose frozen. It does not necessarily mean a perfectly relaxed facial sculpt. |
| Before/after sheet | Labeled neutral beside each isolated key at 1.0, arranged 12 keys per sheet. |
| Delta | Whole-image mean RGB difference from neutral; a coarse change detector, not an emotion score or local deformation measure. |

**Important:** facial controls sometimes appear under Other/System. This library includes every morph, not only author-categorized eyes/brows/lips, so those controls are not silently omitted. Some entries therefore control outfits, visibility, hair or materials rather than facial motion. A missing Eyebrow category does not prove a model has no brow controls.

## 5. Capture methodology

- A separate copy of the app’s Babylon/MMD renderer loaded the actual cached models and their available textures. Production renderer bundles were not replaced.
- Each model was loaded separately, with a deterministic initialization random source. A skeletal base pose was sampled and frozen; automatic face mixing and blinking were disabled for the capture.
- Every morph was reset before setting the next isolated weight. Each key was captured at 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 from the front, plus 1.0 with the camera rotated by +0.4 radians (approximately 22.9°). The oblique view is not a 45° side profile.
- Camera framing was adjusted per rig using head/eye bones and selected fixed fallbacks. The target and radius were held fixed across the model’s control captures. Models therefore have consistent within-model comparisons, not identical physical camera coordinates across characters.
- Lighting and the rendering material setup were kept consistent within each model. Authored materials and model differences prevent assuming equivalent brightness across models.
- New collection images are 480 × 480 captures of actual rendered canvas pixels composited onto white, saved as JPEG quality 94%. The first Jean reference uses 480 × 480 browser PNG screenshots.
- The original Jean images use two-digit indices; the remaining galleries use three-digit indices. Use the actual paths in this document/catalog instead of constructing filenames from assumptions.
- All morphs were captured, including material controls and controls that hide geometry. An unusual, blank or unchanged result for a particular key is not necessarily a capture failure.
- Source model binaries were read locally. Missing public textures were fetched into the isolated reference folder. Some unavailable references were resolved by documented filename/case aliases or matching same-character texture names; provenance is retained in the texture report.
- Source files with unavailable textures remain explicitly flagged. One legacy Nicole model uses substitute gray materials, with additional restrictions below.

### What these captures do not validate

They do not validate anatomical correctness, per-character comfortable maximum weights, ARKit compatibility, semantic emotion labels, expression combinations, motion transitions, gaze behavior, speech synchronization or live microphone performance. No future AI should describe all 4,789 controls as visually calibrated merely because they were captured. Representative expressions were reviewed across the collection; every individual key was not given a human semantic annotation.

## 6. Current facial engine: what exists today

The current MMD face adapter recognizes 11 channels. It normalizes original morph names to lowercase and removes whitespace, underscores, periods and hyphens. It takes the first exact normalized match. For nonvowel channels only, aliases at least five characters long may also match as substrings. It does not match the author English-name field.

| App channel | Original-name aliases |
|---|---|
| a | `あ`, `moutha`, `vrc.v_aa`, `aa`, `a` |
| i | `い`, `mouthi`, `vrc.v_ih`, `ih`, `i` |
| u | `う`, `mouthu`, `vrc.v_ou`, `ou`, `u` |
| e | `え`, `mouthe`, `vrc.v_e`, `e` |
| o | `お`, `moutho`, `vrc.v_oh`, `oh`, `o` |
| blink | `まばたき`, `両目閉じ`, `blink`, `eyesclose`, `eyeclose` |
| smileEyes | `笑い`, `笑顔`, `eyesmile`, `happyeye`, `smileeye` |
| smile | `にやり`, `微笑み`, `mouthsmile`, `smile` |
| sad | `困る`, `悲しい`, `sad`, `troubled`, `worry` |
| angry | `怒り`, `angry`, `mad` |
| surprised | `びっくり`, `驚き`, `surprised`, `surprise` |

The existing `FaceMixer` combines mouth poses with blink and emotion weights and smooths those weights. Happy/amused share smile-related channels; sad/concerned share sad-related channels; the recognized angry channel currently targets zero. Ordinary Edge chat speech may carry LLM-generated mood. Live call performance currently supplies neutral mood. GLB/skeleton-only loading does not attach this MMD face adapter.

Current Edge mouth cues are heuristically derived from spelling inside actual word boundaries; they are not a phoneme-alignment system. OpenAI speech in the reviewed implementation supplies audio-only timing metadata. `rest`/`closed` zero the controlled vowels; `fv` approximates an i weight. These controller pose labels are not guaranteed morph names.

Adapter mappings below are static lookup predictions using the current adapter rules. They are **not** a judgment that a mapped control looks right, that every runtime supports it, or that unrecognized controls are useless.

## 7. Quality caveats and evidence boundaries

- **Legacy Nicole:** original path and matching textures could not be recovered. Its synthetic loader path is not a discovered real asset identifier. Gray substitute materials show geometry changes only. Painted iris/brow details, alpha cutouts and material morph behavior cannot be evaluated from that reference.
- **Mint swimsuit variant:** authored materials appeared unusually bright in the reference renderer. Subtle skin shading and cheek effects are not reliably judged from those captures. The limitation is recorded per model.
- **Unavailable textures:** model-specific lists identify unresolved references. Some referenced files may be unused. A successful render is not proof that every original appearance effect is present.
- **Occlusion:** bangs, glasses, hats and masks remain visible. Hidden facial geometry can change without producing much image difference. Twiggy’s mask particularly obscures mouth evaluation.
- **Pose:** some rigs have a turned or tilted head in the frozen base pose. Front means the chosen frontal camera, not proof of anatomical straight-on alignment.
- **Whole-image deltas:** collection deltas use RGB images downsampled to 120 × 120. The original Jean delta report used full-size PNG measurements. Values are not directly comparable between those two methods.
- **Low-change threshold:** below 0.05 on the mean 0–255 RGB difference scale is flagged as low change. Compression, hair coverage and effect size can influence this. Do not turn this threshold into an automatic “disable key” rule.
- **Semantic labels:** no full per-key visual interpretation, muscle/action-unit mapping or safe-combination matrix has been authored yet. Exact names and images are the evidence.
- **Scope:** only the 50 available cached model binaries were included. Undownloaded catalog models, GLB characters and stage/environment PMX files are outside this library.

## 8. Verification performed

- All 50 original cached model binaries parsed successfully during inventory (48 PMX, 2 BPMX).
- The 49 new capture sets passed file-presence checks, runtime/source morph-name order checks, basic neutral visibility checks and image-difference analysis. The original Jean had its separate capture checks.
- The 50 browser galleries passed navigation, key-count, search/filter, representative-image dimension and page-error checks.
- All generated Markdown reference links were checked to exist.
- Representative neutral/eye/brow/mouth views were visually reviewed across the collection. Author categories are incomplete on some rigs; inspect their Other/System keys too.
- Actual original captures total 19,206. The 422 contact sheets and additional overview/QA images are derived previews and are not included in that capture count.

## 11. Recommended next analysis output

After visually reviewing a selected model, produce a calibration record containing: exact model ID/binary checksum; observed movement per useful key; confidence and occlusion notes; useful weight ranges; left/right behavior; conflicts and corrective combinations; proposed emotion recipes; speech/blink/gaze ownership rules; and validation clips still required. Leave uncertain semantics explicitly unverified. Do not equate maximum deformation with best expressiveness.

## 12. Traceability files

- `AI-FACIAL-REFERENCE-CATALOG.json`: full structured model/control/image catalog.
- `collection/library-report.json`: library counts and per-model summary.
- `collection/validation-report.json`: morph-order, coverage and image-difference checks for the 49 new models.
- `collection/browser-check.json`: browser gallery checks.
- `collection/texture-report.json`: public texture retrieval results and alias provenance; a saved alias may retain the earlier HTTP 404 in its historical error field. Use `status` and `aliasFrom` together.
- Per-model `capture-report.json`, `visual-check.json`, `morphs.json` and `README.md`: underlying evidence/settings where present.
- `implementation-snapshot/`: copies of the six listed current implementation files for interpretation.
- `MANIFEST.json` in the ZIP: file paths, lengths and SHA-256 values for packaged evidence.
